text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over many years, and early symptoms can be very mild or completely absent.

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work overtime to flush out the excess sugar, which pulls water from your tissues and makes you feel constantly thirsty.
Persistent fatigue: When your cells cannot properly absorb glucose for energy, you may feel unusually tired or exhausted even after getting enough rest.
Blurred vision: High blood sugar can cause temporary fluid shifts or swelling in the lens of the eyes.
Slow-healing sores or cuts: Elevated blood sugar impairs circulation and weakens the immune response, making minor wounds take much longer to heal.
Tingling or numbness: Peripheral nerve damage (neuropathy) can start as a mild tingling, burning, or loss of sensation in the hands or feet.
Frequent infections: Bacteria and fungi thrive on excess sugar, leading to recurring urinary tract infections (UTIs), yeast infections, or skin issues.
Unexplained weight changes: You may experience unexpected weight loss (as the body starts burning fat and muscle for energy) or gradual weight gain tied to insulin resistance.
Darkened skin patches: A condition called acanthosis nigricans causes velvety, dark patches of skin to form around the neck, armpits, or groin, signaling underlying insulin resistance.
